President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as part of efforts to expand agricultural financing and improve access to affordable loans for farmers and businesses across the agricultural value chain. The APC Presidential Campaign Council, in a statement by its spokesperson and Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, on Sunday, said the recapitalisation would strengthen the bank’s financial capacity to support farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors and aggregators. The APC PCC stated, “President Bola Tinubu’s administration has committed N450bn to agricultural financing programmes to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria. “Through the Bank of Agriculture, the administration has reached over 500,000 smallholder farmers, and the President has also approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda. “The Federal Government, under President Tinubu, went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain. “The interventions demonstrated President Tinubu’s commitment to transforming agriculture into a major driver of economic growth, food security, and job creation.” It added that the initiative was aimed at expanding the bank’s reach to underserved farming communities and mobilising more resources for domestic food production. The ruling party’s Campaign Council stated, “The ₦450bn agricultural financing intervention, support for more than 500,000 smallholder farmers, and the planned ₦1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture represent a significant commitment to building a more productive and resilient agricultural sector. It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds. “The initiative aims to reach two million farmers and distribute more than 10 million bags of fertiliser. “The intervention was particularly significant in Northern Nigeria, where agriculture remains a major source of livelihood and economic activity. “States including Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe, and Bauchi are among the areas receiving attention under the programme.” The APC Presidential Campaign Council said the Bank of Agriculture had procured about 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava under its N200bn Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme to stabilise commodity markets and protect farmers from distress sales. The APC Presidential Campaign Council said the Bank of Agriculture had introduced an Onion Financing Programme in partnership with NOPPMAN, which represents over 11,800 farmers, to boost production and market access. It added that the bank would cover 70 per cent of farmers’ input costs, while cooperatives would contribute the remaining 30 per cent. The APC PCC stated, “Other agricultural initiatives the bank is implementing include dry-season farming financing, mechanisation, ginger recovery, women’s cooperative financing, youth participation, and commercial poultry production. “Under the dry-season agricultural financing programme, the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle. “The initiative includes financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat cultivation and another 300,000 hectares for crops including rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava, and soybeans. “The Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has also supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds, recovered more than 9,000 bags for multiplication, and is planning an expansion across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.” The APC PCC said the Bank of Agriculture was targeting 50,000 women nationwide with insured cooperative loans at nine per cent interest. It continued, “Under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme, 1,571 tractors have been deployed to 23 states. “The tractors are expected to mechanise 1.2 million hectares of farmland, with access provided to farming communities through qualified Mechanisation Service Providers. “Other interventions include a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme, which provides 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families.” Ahead of the January 16, 2027, presidential election, President Bola Tinubu is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC. In preparation for the poll, the APC Presidential Campaign Council has continued to highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors.
